citations.narrative:
- A cage housing 5 cockatiels had multiple sharp points present in the enclosure. Sharp points are a potential source of
injury or entrapment to the birds. Primary enclosures must contain no sharp points or edges that could injure the birds.
Corrected at the time of inspection

- At least 9 cages are missing appropriate perches for the birds. Most cages have broad wooden perch structures present
- however, these are not the appropriate size and shape to serve as routine cockatiel perches. Lack of appropriate
perches can be a source of distress and discomfort to birds that normally perch. The licensee must ensure that there are
perches available that are appropriate to the age and species of birds housed therein and a sufficient number of perches
of appropriate size, shape, strength, texture, and placement to comfortably hold all the birds in the primary enclosure at
the same time.
Correct by: 1 November 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
